bullets.title: AI infrastructure debt/credit stress emerges as third macro pressure point
bullets.body: Citi and 22V flag credit concerns as a new macro headwind alongside oil and rates: AI neoclouds (CRWV, ORCL) face ~16% unsecured bond yields and OpenAI concentration risk, Nscale lost MSFT and saw IPO valuation collapse from ~$30B to $16-19B on execution failures, and Anthropic's IPO was repriced from $2T+ to $1.5T. Goldman hosted a cross-cap investor call specifically addressing the AI infrastructure sell-off and higher cost-of-capital implications for capex buildout. Data center bond yields have risen from <5% to ~7%, with securitization approaching 8%.

bullets.title: Last week's AI/tech tape was severe: SMH -10.5%, AI basket -12.5% to -16.5% w/w
bullets.body: The MS AI Tech Beneficiaries basket (MSXXAIB) fell 16.5% w/w—worst week since launch in early 2023—with Global Memory -18% w/w, SMH -10.5%, and NDX -5.5%. SPX P/E is now 15% lower YTD while 12-month forward EPS is up 31%. Citi notes credit concerns, oil, and rates as three simultaneous pressure points; Hedgeye counts 26 of 35 AI bubble names signaling bearish trends with shorts outnumbering longs 3-to-1.

bullets.title: S&P bouncing Monday morning (+0.8%) but technicals remain fragile; 7,600 is the line
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures opened +0.48% to 7,741 with semis leading (SOXX +3.77%) on CRWV/INTC upgrades, and the index was trading +0.8% at 7,723 by mid-morning. Hedgeye pegs NASDAQ trend support at 26,119 and S&P support at 7,601 with resistance at 7,725; Piper sees path of least resistance lower with a likely retest of 7,600. S&P weekly MACD is rolling over—the 7th such occurrence since 2017—and prior instances were followed by material declines. VIX rose 11.6% to 17.67 intraday.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: Quality factor at 52-week high as mid-cycle transition tightens financial conditions
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson notes the quality factor is up ~6% since mid-August while equal-weight S&P 500 is down ~4%, with earnings revisions spread between high and low quality at ~10%—second-widest since 2010. Financial conditions (rates, dollar, energy) are at their tightest since 2022, and economically sensitive sectors (Financials, Materials, Discretionary, Industrials) are down ~10% since mid-August. Historically, quality outperforms by an average 7.5% over the following 12 months at similar revision spreads.

bullets.title: Rates remain a headwind: 10-year at 5.10%, Fed on hold, core CPI re-accelerating
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.10% (+2 bps Monday morning) with Hedgeye's cycle high target at 5.34%. Core CPI printed +0.33% m/m vs. 0.2% consensus (2.57% y/y), and October CPI nowcast rose 14 bps. The Fed is expected to remain on hold in October, with committee members emphasizing patience. Hedgeye maintains bond shorts; Piper notes nominal GDP running at 6%+, well above Fed Funds, keeping inflation sticky.

bullets.title: Oil above $100 for 7 straight days; Brent signaling potential cycle high at $110-111
bullets.body: WTI front-month has closed above $100 for seven straight days at a new high, with the April contract rising from ~$82 to ~$92. Hedgeye maintains Brent crude and natural gas longs, flagging potential cycle highs at $110-111 for Brent. XLE has broken out above September highs. Diesel prices are up 127% year-over-year per Hedgeye's CPI nowcast data.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex trajectory is the week's central earnings question
bullets.body: JPMorgan's TMT preview flags hyperscaler capex guidance and evidence of AI monetization ROI as the key investor demand this earnings season. AMZN CEO Jassy told Ben Horowitz AWS is sold out of compute past 2028; AMZN is increasing 2026-28 NVDA GPU purchases to 3M chips adding ~2GW/1GW in 2027/28. MS raised AMZN to Top Pick ($350 PT, +33% upside) forecasting AWS at $164.5B of 2028 EBIT. META's every 100M Muse DAUs requires 1-4GW of GPU capacity, and MSFT FY27 capex is expected above $220B.

bullets.title: Data center buildout targeting 51GW in FY27 but faces power, permitting, and community resistance
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis forecasts FY27 global data center additions of ~51.2GW (>2x FY26's 25GW), with US net additions +110% y/y to 38GW. However, at least 47 of the largest projects are delayed, withdrawn, or blocked in 2026; over 1,000 US communities have introduced moratoria; and Bernstein estimates only ~35% of the planned US pipeline is credible. Five-year Treasury yields are up >100bps since January, pushing data center bond yields from <5% to ~7% and securitization yields toward 8%.

bullets.title: NAHB hits cycle low of 29—weakest since 2012—flagging earnings breadth may be peaking
bullets.body: The October NAHB Housing Market Index fell 3 points to 29, the lowest reading since 2012, with all three components declining m/m and three of four regions showing weakness. Piper's macro team reads this as a signal that EPS growth and earnings breadth are likely peaking, with interest-rate-sensitive areas correlating with NAHB deterioration. The S&P path of least resistance is lower with a likely retest of 7,600 support.

bullets.title: Jefferies quant argues AI earnings deceleration to 30% in 2027 makes ex-AI rotation attractive
bullets.body: Jefferies quant team projects AI earnings growth decelerates from ~100% in 2026 to 30% in 2027 and 22% in 2028, while AI trades at 23x forward P/E vs. ex-AI sectors at 13x (below long-term average). AI returns slowed to only 6% in H2 2026 vs. 32% in H1. Most attractive ex-AI opportunities: healthcare services, transport, biotech; DM Europe shows the clearest differential with AI at 29x vs. ex-AI at 13x.

bullets.title: CXMT 4F² DRAM roadmap rattles memory stocks; ASML raising 2027 equipment prices
bullets.body: Chinese memory maker CXMT announced plans to commercialize 4F² DRAM within the year, triggering selloffs in Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron on Chinese supply-overhang concerns, though mass-production viability remains unverified. Separately, ASML is raising equipment prices in 2027 amid AI-driven demand that has filled its order book through 2030; ASML projects a 77% rise in AI spend in 2026 with full-year sales guidance of €44-45B.

bullets.title: Sector rotation underway: semis/hardware being sold, software/IT services and healthcare receiving inflows
bullets.body: Piper's macro strategist is rotating out of semiconductors and hardware into software and IT services. Healthcare sector ratio to S&P 500 is at its highest since February, with Goldman clients net buying HC at the fastest pace in 6+ months. Institutional active positioning in Tech was at a 5-year high pre-selloff; Utilities, Materials, and Industrials remain at 5-year lows. Hedgeye is maintaining MSFT, AAPL, and META as preferred tech longs while shorting AI infrastructure names.

bullets.title: On-prem hardware repatriation: enterprise open-weight AI model deployment benefits DELL, HPE
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's CIO survey shows enterprises deploying open-weight models on proprietary on-prem hardware for security and control, driving a 'repatriation' trend. DELL and HPE are positioned to benefit from the shift away from cloud-only deployments, with on-prem strength partly driven by pull-forward demand and pricing dynamics.

bullets.title: Comms/digital ads entering earnings with clear headwinds: Google CTR falling, META Muse DAU drop
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Q4 comms themes call flags Google Search click-through falling in every segment of agency benchmarks in Q3 as AI Overviews scale; Google Cloud consensus needs 92% 2027 growth. Meta AI Muse lost 42% of US weekly users within 3 weeks of launch with monetization unclear; Meta CPMs did step up from early September. Reddit worldwide web traffic grew only 4.1% in September (slowest in 21 months), and Netflix global Top-10 viewing hours fell 11% in Q3.

bullets.title: US midterm elections add policy uncertainty; 35 data center ballot measures on Nov 3 ballot
bullets.body: Approximately 35 data center ballot measures will appear on the November 3 ballot across 8 states, with Texas and Ohio senate/gubernatorial races carrying data center zoning implications (Texas represents ~35% of announced IT capacity through 2030). OPCO notes cross-asset macro signals are not yet indicating a 'Quad 4' regime, but SPX must retake 7,700 with VIX declining to build confidence in equity recovery.

bullets.title: Hedgeye ETF re-rank: XLK sold, QQQ cut to minimum; RSP and equal-weight added
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough sold 50bps each of UUP, DBMF, TOPT, BUG, and XLK (XLK dropped 12 spots in one week to rank 19th). He added RSP and RISR at minimums, reflecting a rotation away from tech-heavy/momentum ETFs toward equal-weight and rate-hedge positioning. QQQ fell from rank 5 on Oct 13 to rank 16 on Oct 19.

bullets.title: Business travel budgets expected +10% in 2027; inbound US travel recovering but still negative
bullets.body: UBS leisure/travel weekly notes hotel booking volumes are up 9% and negotiated room rates up 4%, with business travel budgets expected to rise ~10% in 2027—the most optimistic survey for US-exposed travel names. Separately, Hedgeye notes inbound travel improved to -4.3% in September vs. -11.8% in August, suggesting gradual recovery in international visitors.

bullets.title: EPS beats strong but sales beats at record low; quality earnings divergence widening
bullets.body: 22V notes a 77.6% EPS beat rate but a record-low 33.3% sales beat rate at the S&P index level. Russell 2000 3Q26 aggregate earnings are leading 53.7% above expectations (85.6% ex-financials). MS notes the earnings revisions spread between high and low quality is at ~10%—second-widest since 2010—with quality's relative valuation near historical median despite the revisions advantage.

bullets.title: Starlink US app downloads +91% in Q3 (record); SpaceX buying spectrum to become US carrier
bullets.body: Starlink US app downloads hit a record +91% in Q3 as SpaceX's recent spectrum purchase from Grain positions it to become a US mobile carrier. Separately, European MNOs (Vodafone, Telefonica, Orange) signed an LOI to jointly bid for MSS spectrum for D2D service, with AST Spacemobile holding existing deals with all three carriers but no satellite partner yet selected.
